source: Experiment H design.json; arm A (production, roster off) outputs
draw_rule: All production-selected deaths are included. From the unselected pool, random.Random(seed) shuffles the sorted list of matches that have an unselected death; the first N matches are kept and, in that order, rng.choice picks one death from each match's sorted unselected deaths.

categories.A: Already available: a concrete field holds the fact for this death. a_location=view if it is in the CoachLlmView the model receives (e.g. death, clock, low_ink, map, related, importance); a_location=pipeline if it is in ScenarioContext or the vision manifest but not in the view (e.g. special, score, zone_control, map.ink, players).
categories.B: Derivable: computable from readings or fused state that exist today, with no new detector (e.g. special ready when the fight began, from special gauge readings and the death time).
categories.C: New detector required: visible on screen but not extracted (e.g. the weapon that splatted you, the splat feed).
categories.D: Not realistically observable: needs information the footage does not carry or substantially harder inference (e.g. off-screen teammate positions, opponent intent).

primary_rule: Exactly one primary category per fact. When more than one applies, the category needing the least engineering work wins: A before B before C before D, and within A, view before pipeline.
evidence_rule: A: field path and its value for this death. B: the existing readings or state it is computed from. C: the screen element. D: the reason.
decision_rule: Counts are per missing fact, not per death. Actionable facts are A, B and C; D facts are recorded only. If A + B >= C, the next experiment targets the theme with the most A + B facts (ties: more A facts, then report both); within that theme the most common of A-view, A-pipeline and B decides its kind (ties: least work first): A-view -> prompt / claim-catalog experiment, A-pipeline -> view-extension experiment, B -> fusion feature. If C > A + B, scope a detector for the theme with the most C facts. Ranking review is flagged if unselected deaths average at least 1.0 more A + B missing facts per death than selected deaths (descriptive; no automatic change).
